closest_prior_work: Luo et al. — Semantics-Based Obfuscation-Resilient Binary Diffing (IEEE TIFS 2017)
Bayer et al. — TTAnalyze / Scalable Behavior-Based Malware Clustering (NDSS 2009)
Yamaguchi et al. — Joern / Code Property Graphs (IEEE S&P 2014)
novelty_gap: No prior work defines (1) a formally specified, multi-dimensional, normalized pseudometric on execution-trace-derived behavioral features with dimension-specific distance justifications and explicit metric-space assumptions, (2) a versioned, queryable longitudinal behavioral genome tracking a program's full behavioral profile across its entire release history, or (3) a test-suite-free regression oracle using unsupervised behavioral distance — the last being empirically unvalidated but novel as a claim. All prior behavioral fingerprinting is malware-oriented and one-shot; all prior regression verification is formal/static and language-specific; all prior multi-representation systems (Joern, ProGraML) are static. The dynamic behavioral pseudometric analog with formal properties does not exist in any reviewed prior work.
novelty_verdict_justification: Two claims survive all adversarial attacks with HIGH confidence (S1: formal behavioral pseudometric; S2: longitudinal behavioral genome). One claim is novel but empirically unproven (S3: test-suite-free regression oracle — H5). One claim is credible but narrower than originally stated (S4: cross-language equivalence, restricted to 3–5 of 8 dimensions due to unresolved OP-4 and OP-6). One claim is a vision claim only (S5: behavioral supply-chain artifact). The project has a legitimate and non-redundant contribution; it requires sharpening around S1, S2, and — after empirical validation — S3. Path to STRONG verdict: validate H5 empirically and confirm the multi-dimensional structure outperforms all single-dimension baselines.
statistical_notes: Bonferroni-corrected alpha = 0.0017 for H1-H6. Non-parametric tests (Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis, McNemar, DeLong) specified per hypothesis. Bootstrap 95% CI required on all primary metrics. Power analysis re-run at alpha = 0.0017 in BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md §7.1: minimum test pairs = 800, recommended test pairs = 1280. Consistent with RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md.
major_threats: IV-05: Non-determinism and execution flakiness — Assumption A6 (determinism) is violated by the majority of production software; intra-version genome variance has not been measured
IV-04: Rare-trigger behavioral differences are undetectable — bugs triggered by mu_I(Delta) ~= 0 inputs will never be sampled from I_prod regardless of D
EV-02: Long-running, interactive, and distributed programs are out of scope — timeout-bounded extraction cannot capture behaviors over long horizons
CV-01: D(G1,G2) does not certify semantic equivalence — Rice's theorem; D is an empirical approximation only
CV-05: Cross-language behavioral equivalence (H3/H4) depends on unresolved OP-4 — no formal cross-language procedure alignment exists for CONTROL dimension
EV-03: Functional and logic paradigms are not supported — CONTROL dimension (g_C) is definitionally OO/imperative-centric
IV-01: Structural similarity may confound behavioral similarity — CONTROL and EXECUTION dimensions derived from control-flow structure
IV-02: Oracle/ground-truth reliability — Defects4J labels depend on test coverage; genuine SBG detections may count as false positives
IV-03: Measurement bias from dynamic analysis instrumentation — probe effect on TEMPORAL/RESOURCE dimensions
EV-04: Scalability — GED for CONTROL is NP-hard; heap isomorphism for STATE is GI-hard; results on small benchmarks may not imply tractability on large programs
unmitigable_threats: CV-01: D(G1,G2) does not certify semantic equivalence (Rice's theorem — undecidability; OP-2 unresolved)
IV-04-residual: Rare-trigger behavioral differences are undetectable under finite sampling from I_prod
EV-02-residual: Long-running, interactive, and distributed programs are out of scope by definition
EV-03-residual: Functional and logic paradigms are not supported without a formal CONTROL dimension extension
CV-05-residual: Full 8-dimension cross-language comparison blocked by OP-4 (no formal cross-language procedure alignment)
open_problems_blocking_phase_1: OP-1: Minimum sample size N* for reliable genome estimation — assumed N=200 pending SH-3 validation; must be confirmed before H1-H6 experiments
OP-4: Cross-language procedure alignment for CONTROL dimension — blocks full H4 claim; H4 must be restricted to g_D + g_X + exploratory g_C until resolved
OP-6: Temporal normalization across architectures — blocks cross-language TEMPORAL/RESOURCE comparison; these dimensions must be excluded from cross-language experiments
open_problems_non_blocking: OP-2: Decidability of epsilon-semantic equivalence for finite programs
OP-3: Confidence-weighted genome distance D_conf (Welch t-statistic analog)
OP-5: Principled heap abstraction selection for STATE dimension
unresolved_questions: What is the intra-version genome variance Var[G(P)] for the benchmark programs? (must be measured as a noise floor before any inter-version claim)

Does the 8-dimensional structured distance outperform a learned behavioral embedding trained on execution trace features? (Attack 7 settling experiment — required for publication, not for Phase 1 start)

Does the multi-dimensional architecture outperform all single-dimension baselines on Defects4J? (Attack 3 ablation — this is H6 and is a Phase 1 experiment, but the answer determines whether the architecture is justified on discriminability or interpretability grounds)
What fraction of Defects4J regressions are rare-trigger (mu_I(Delta) < 0.01)? (SH-2 stratification — determines realistic H5 recall ceiling under I_prod)

cross_document_inconsistencies.description: Hypothesis numbering mismatch between FORMAL_MODEL.md (H1-H6) and RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md (H1-H6). Labels H2, H3, H4, H6 are assigned to different hypotheses in each document. FORMAL_MODEL H2=Sensitivity, RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES H2=Outperforms Baselines. FORMAL_MODEL H3=Cross-Language, RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES H3=Robustness Under Refactoring. FORMAL_MODEL H4=Versioning, RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES H4=Cross-Language. FORMAL_MODEL H6=Uniqueness, RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES H6=Multi-Dimensional Value.
cross_document_inconsistencies.resolution: Adopt FORMAL_MODEL.md H-numbering as canonical before Phase 1 begins. Update all downstream documents to use consistent labels.

cross_document_inconsistencies.description: RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md H4 (Cross-Language) includes g_C as a primary portable dimension. NOVELTY_ANALYSIS.md Attack 4 and THREATS_TO_VALIDITY.md CV-05 both establish that g_C is problematic cross-language due to unresolved OP-4 (no cross-language procedure alignment). The effective cross-language portable dimension set should be {g_D, g_X} with g_C as exploratory/partial, not a confirmed primary dimension.
cross_document_inconsistencies.resolution: Update RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md H4 to list {g_D, g_X} as confirmed portable dimensions and g_C as exploratory. Explicitly mark g_T, g_R, g_U as excluded from all cross-language comparisons.

cross_document_inconsistencies.description: BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md does not specify a cross-language equivalent pair count in its minimum viable table. RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md H4 requires at least 35 equivalent pairs per language pair (5 language pairs = 175 minimum cross-language pairs). This count is absent from BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md §7.
cross_document_inconsistencies.resolution: Add cross-language equivalent pair count to BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md minimum viable table: 175 minimum (35 per language pair x 5 pairs), 250 recommended.

cross_document_inconsistencies.description: BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md does not describe a real-repository version history corpus for FORMAL_MODEL H4 / SH-4 (monotonicity). RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md SH-4 requires 10 GitHub projects with >=100 commits each. This corpus is entirely missing from BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md scope.
cross_document_inconsistencies.resolution: Add a separate SH-4 corpus section to BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md specifying 10 GitHub projects with >=100 commits; or document as a separate Phase 1 corpus preparation task.

cross_document_inconsistencies.description: Statistical significance threshold mismatch: BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md §7.1 power analysis uses alpha = 0.05 for sample size derivation; RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md uses Bonferroni-corrected alpha = 0.0017 for all H1-H6 tests. The minimum viable test set (400 pairs) is powered for alpha = 0.05, not alpha = 0.0017. Under the corrected alpha, power may be insufficient at 400 pairs.
cross_document_inconsistencies.resolution: BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md must re-run McNemar power analysis at alpha = 0.0017. If 400 pairs is insufficient, increase target or explicitly accept lower power and document the limitation.

cross_document_inconsistencies.description: FORMAL_MODEL.md H6 is 'Behavioral Genome Uniqueness' (collision rate). RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md H6 is 'Multi-Dimensional Value' (dimension ablation). These are different hypotheses with the same label. The uniqueness claim is addressed in RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md only as RQ10 (exploratory), not as a confirmatory hypothesis.
cross_document_inconsistencies.resolution: Rename RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md H6 to H6-MV and add H6-U for uniqueness/collision as a separate confirmatory hypothesis mapped to FORMAL_MODEL H6. Reconcile with canonical H-numbering from INC-1 resolution.

cross_document_inconsistencies.description: threats_summary.json severity_counts conflates initial severity with residual severity. Fourteen entries marked 'HIGH' include entries with residual_risk = 'MEDIUM' after mitigation. Two entries (EV-02, CV-05) have residual_risk = 'HIGH' (fundamental/unmitigable) but are categorized alongside mitigable threats.
cross_document_inconsistencies.resolution: Distinguish initial severity from residual risk in all downstream threat tracking. For Phase 1 prioritization, use residual risk.

recommendation: CONDITIONAL PASS. Phase 0 has produced a formally grounded research foundation: a precise research question, a complete formal model with 22 definitions and 6 hypotheses, a comprehensive prior art survey (40 works across 10 domains), a rigorous adversarial novelty review (MODERATE verdict with two HIGH-confidence surviving claims), a detailed threats analysis (32 threats, 5 unmitigable), operationalized hypotheses with power analyses, and a statistically justified benchmark design. However, three conditions must be satisfied before Phase 1 execution begins: (1) the hypothesis numbering must be canonicalized — the current H1-H6 mismatch between FORMAL_MODEL.md and RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md is a critical execution risk; (2) the intra-version genome variance (noise floor) must be measured as a preliminary experiment before any inter-version distance is interpreted; (3) BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md must be updated to include cross-language pair counts and must re-run the power analysis at alpha = 0.0017. All five unmitigable threats must be disclosed as scope limitations in any publication. The cross-language hypothesis (FORMAL_MODEL H3 / RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES H4) must be formally marked as exploratory/preliminary until OP-4 is resolved.
fixes_applied: FIX-1 (resolves INC-1): FORMAL_MODEL.md H2-H6 relabeled to match canonical numbering from master SBG prompt. H2 is now 'Structured SBG Discriminative Power Over Baselines', H3 is now 'Behavioral Genome Robustness Under Refactoring', H4 is now 'Cross-Language Behavioral Generalization', H5 is now 'Behavioral Genome Regression Detection', H6 is now 'Multi-Dimensional Behavioral Value'. Formal mathematical content preserved; headings and cross-references updated. RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md verified as already matching canonical numbering — no changes required.

FIX-2 (resolves INC-2): RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md H4 portable dimension set changed from {g_C, g_D, g_X} to {g_D, g_X} (confirmed portable). g_C marked EXPLORATORY/PRELIMINARY with explicit note citing OP-4 (cross-language procedure alignment is an unresolved open problem). Primary D_xlang test statistic now uses only {g_D, g_X} with w_D = w_X = 1/2. FORMAL_MODEL.md H4 (formerly H3) updated to explicitly state g_C is excluded from primary confirmatory test with EXPLORATORY label. g_T, g_R, g_U explicitly excluded from cross-language comparisons.

FIX-3 (resolves INC-5): BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md §7.1 power analysis updated to use Bonferroni-corrected alpha = 0.0017 (= 0.01/6). Calculation shown explicitly: z_alpha/2 = 3.12; required discordant pairs scale by ratio (3.120+0.842)^2/(1.960+0.842)^2 = 15.70/7.85 = 2.0x; minimum test pairs updated from 400 to 800; recommended test pairs updated from 640 to 1280. Total pair counts scaled accordingly: minimum_viable_total_pairs updated from 2000 to 4000; target_total_pairs updated from 3200 to 6400. artifacts/research/benchmark_design_summary.json updated to reflect all revised counts and the corrected statistical parameters.
phase_1_prerequisites: 1. Canonicalize hypothesis numbering: adopt FORMAL_MODEL.md H1-H6 labels throughout all documents (resolves INC-1)

2. Update RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md H4 (Cross-Language) to explicitly restrict portable dimensions to {g_D, g_X} with g_C exploratory; exclude g_T, g_R, g_U from all cross-language comparisons (resolves INC-2)
3. Add cross-language pair count (175 minimum, 250 recommended) to BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md minimum viable table (resolves INC-3)
4. Document SH-4 version history corpus (10 GitHub projects, >=100 commits) as a separate corpus specification in BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md or as a standalone corpus preparation task (resolves INC-4)
5. Re-run BENCHMARK_DESIGN.md McNemar power analysis at alpha = 0.0017; confirm test set size or adjust targets accordingly (resolves INC-5)
6. Pre-register primary hypotheses H1 and H5 (regression oracle) at OSF or AsPredicted before any genome extraction begins (addresses CL-02)
7. Execute SH-3 (convergence rate experiment) first to confirm N = 200 is sufficient; no H1-H6 experiments start until N is empirically validated (addresses OP-1)
8. Measure intra-version genome variance Var[G(P)] as a preliminary experiment on the benchmark corpus before any inter-version D comparisons are reported (addresses IV-05 noise floor)

9. Define and document the containerized reproducibility environment (OS version, compiler, runtime, PRNG = 42, locale = UTF-8, timezone = UTC, thread policy) before first genome extraction run (addresses RL-01)

10. Formally mark FORMAL_MODEL H3 / H4 (Cross-Language) as exploratory/preliminary in all Phase 1 documentation until OP-4 is resolved; do not include it in the primary confirmatory hypothesis list for any publication (addresses CV-05 and INC-2)

11. All claims must be framed as empirical approximations, not semantic decision procedures; D(G1,G2) < theta predicts behavioral equivalence probabilistically — it does not certify it (addresses CV-01)

12. Scope limitations must be explicitly stated: single-process, non-interactive, bounded execution (T_max = 30s), deterministic programs under controlled execution, imperative/OO paradigms only (addresses EV-02, EV-03)
